Rationale: The minimal invariant D-1 violated: Mirror addressed data files by PATH while dedup handed that address to rows meaning 'these exact bytes' (defect review 2026-08-24).
AcceptanceCriteria: Across a multi-run timeline that edits one of two duplicate files, a byte census of the pool shows no claimed DataPath whose bytes changed, and the prior snapshot restores the old content for every path that shared it.

Title: Dedup covers content first seen within one run
Requirement: Content with the same (xxH2Hash,Length) appearing several times in a single run shall be stored once, with every logical name referencing that one physical object.
Rationale: D-5: the dedup lookup consulted only the PRIOR backup, so identical files first seen in one run were each stored in full (Mirror) or copied twice over one name (HashAddressed).
AcceptanceCriteria: Two identical files first seen in one run produce exactly one physical pool file, one distinct DataPath across their rows, and one copy/compress operation.

Title: A legacy-form store is refused, not converted or restored
Requirement: The system shall not re-form data already stored: changing CompressEnabled shall govern only content written after the change, leaving existing objects in the form they were stored in. A manifest row recorded in the legacy Original (path-addressed) form shall fail its backup set before any mutation, naming the condition and the remedy (back up to a fresh BackupPath); -Action Verify shall report it as a finding rather than refuse. Both restorers shall apply the same refusal before writing anything: a manifest row carrying StoredAsHashSize='Original', a manifest witness declaring a format version below the one this build writes, or a non-blank DataPath in a RETIRED grammar - one containing a path separator, or one carrying the base-85 form's space at index 16 - shall abort the restore with the precondition exit code and no file written. The engine shall refuse the same three conditions before mutating a store. There is no read path for a pre-content-addressed store in this kit.
Rationale: Human rulings 2026-08-25: no store exists that must be maintained (so the Original->Hash conversion is deleted rather than made safe), and retroactive space reclamation - in either direction - is not required (so the compression-flip migration goes with it, to a deferred standalone re-pack script if ever wanted). A mixed-form store is already normal because compression is per-file (SR-004), and every row's Compressed describes its OWN object, so nothing downstream needs re-forming. Deleting the migration also deletes a risk class: every migration is a mass rewrite of a store that currently works. Read support was withdrawn 2026-08-26 (human ruling) rather than left as an untested claim: WP9's independent review found the bash half of 'both restorers still restore a legacy store' had no fixture (MIN-2), and the honest resolution was to drop the promise, not to build a fixture for a capability nobody needs -- no such store is known to exist. WP12 extended the refusal from PATH-addressed stores to pre-WP12 CONTENT-addressed ones, whose objects carry the old base-85 space-separated names: StoredAsHashSize cannot tell those apart because a base-85 store also says 'Hash'. Two discriminators, because neither is complete alone - the witness version is present on every modern store but optional on older ones (SR-039 lets a witness-less store restore with a warning), and a structural name test cannot classify a blank DataPath, which is the supported 'recover by hash' state. The residual gap - a witness-less store whose every row is blank - is benign: the locators match CONTENT, never names, so such a store restores correctly whatever its objects are called. The structural test is a POSITIVE test for the retired grammars, NOT the negation of SR-069's. Those are not complements, and conflating them is a defect the suite caught during WP12 implementation: a merely DAMAGED DataPath (the DanglingDataPath class, or a name rewritten by something outside the tool) parses under neither grammar, and SR-049/SR-053/SR-056 require the per-row audit, heal and verify machinery to answer for it. A negative test refused the whole store instead, turning one repairable row into an unrestorable backup. Refuse the old FORMAT; repair damaged ROWS. It still subsumes the pre-WP9 path-separator test, which is one of the two positive shapes.
AcceptanceCriteria: Flipping CompressEnabled re-forms no existing object; new content follows the new setting; the mixed-form store restores byte-exact through both restorers and audits CLEAN. A store whose manifest carries StoredAsHashSize='Original' fails -Action Backup with the fresh-BackupPath remedy and nothing staged or mutated, and yields a finding with a non-zero status under -Action Verify. A constructed legacy store is refused by BOTH restorers with exit 2, naming the cause, with nothing written into the restore target. A constructed pre-WP12 base-85 store is refused by BOTH restorers with exit 2 and nothing written - by its witness version, and again with the witness removed, by its DataPath shape. A store holding a merely DAMAGED DataPath is NOT refused: it still audits, heals and restores through the per-row machinery. The residual gap is demonstrated benign, not merely argued: a store with every object renamed into the retired grammar, every DataPath blanked and no witness still restores byte-exact.

Title: Generated browse view
Requirement: When BrowseView is 'index' the system shall generate a manifest-derived browse view OUTSIDE both roots - INDEX.tsv always, plus per-folder INDEX.html pages and a root search page - covering every logical path including duplicate siblings, refreshed when the canonical manifest ROWS it mirrors change (a SHA-256 of those rows is stamped into .viewstamp - NOT the manifest witness, because a manifest-identical run can rewrite the file with different CSV quoting) and on -Action View; no engine or restore path shall read it.
Rationale: Replaces Mirror's browsability, which was its only real value (human ruling 2026-08-24; the per-folder scaling shape approved 2026-08-25 after a single flat page was measured at ~100 MB for a 500k-file library).
AcceptanceCriteria: The view's entries equal the manifest's RelativePath set exactly, each named RelativePath+('.7z' when the ROW's Compressed is Yes); a stale row-digest triggers a rebuild; -Action View is idempotent; Verify, prune accounting and both restorers ignore the view entirely.

Title: Configuration contract v2
Requirement: The JSON configuration contract shall declare ConfigVersion 2; PreserveFolderTree shall be refused BY NAME in every configuration format; BrowseView (off|index, with link reserved and refused) and ViewPath shall be accepted, ViewPath refused when it is not on the backup volume, or OVERLAPS any path the set owns - BackupPath, ChangePath, SourcePath or SourceStatePath - in EITHER direction (inside one, equal to one, or containing one). The view generator shall additionally refuse to wipe a view root holding anything that is not a generated view. AMENDED 2026-09-01 (WP17, SR-081): CompressProbe (off|excluded-extensions|always, default always) joins the closed per-set key set with its exact-lowercase vocabulary, validated in both configuration formats. This requirement additionally RATIFIES the additive-optional-key policy, so the next optional key does not re-open the question: an OPTIONAL key that carries a default may join contract v2 WITHOUT a version bump, because an unchanged v2 document keeps its meaning exactly; and an OLDER build rejecting that key by name is the CLOSED SCHEMA WORKING AS DESIGNED, not a compatibility break. A key that is required, that removes or re-types an existing key, or that changes the meaning of an unchanged document shall still bump ConfigVersion.
Rationale: Mirror is gone, so a stale config must fail loudly rather than be silently reinterpreted. CLIXML is exempt from SR-042's closed schema, so without an explicit refusal PreserveFolderTree there would be silently ignored.
AcceptanceCriteria: A config carrying PreserveFolderTree fails with status 2 naming the key, in BOTH JSON and CLIXML; an out-of-vocabulary BrowseView and each ViewPath placement violation fail by name, including a ViewPath that CONTAINS a storage root or IS the source tree (WP9 review MAJ-1: those shapes deleted the store and the source respectively, on a run that reported success); and a view root holding ordinary user files is refused rather than wiped. An out-of-vocabulary or mixed-case CompressProbe fails by name in BOTH formats, while a v2 config carrying no CompressProbe key at all loads unchanged and resolves to always with ConfigVersion still 2.

Title: Store audits scale linearly
Requirement: The unreferenced-data-file audit shall be linear in manifest rows plus on-disk data files.
Rationale: Test-BackupManifest re-pipes the whole manifest per on-disk file (O(N^2)) and runs on every backup via Sync step 6; at 500k files it plausibly never finishes.
AcceptanceCriteria: With 10k manifest rows and 10k pool files the audit completes within the harness budget and reports the findings the quadratic implementation reported, with one deliberate difference: existence is decided from the enumerated data-file set, which skips ROOT-LEVEL infrastructure names, so a row whose DataPath is a root-level infrastructure name is blanked rather than kept. No build can produce such a row (the hash-name grammar cannot spell one) and a legacy store is refused first (SR-061), so the case is unreachable rather than merely unlikely.

Title: Empty directories and folder attributes are recorded and restored
Requirement: The system shall record, beside each manifest, one row per source directory that contains no file anywhere beneath it or carries any of the folder attributes Hidden, System, ReadOnly or NotContentIndexed, and both restorers shall recreate those directories and (on Windows) re-apply those attributes after all file content is written and verified. The record shall be advisory: it shall not be witnessed, and an absent, unreadable or malformed record shall leave the pre-existing behaviour and shall never fail a restore. A directory the walk could not enumerate shall not be recorded. On a POSIX host the directories shall be created and the inapplicable attributes reported, not silently dropped.
Rationale: MANIFEST.csv has one row per FILE, so an empty directory was never recreated and a Hidden or System FOLDER came back ordinary (reproduced 2026-08-25, documented in README as a known gap). Ruled 2026-08-26: option B, a small sidecar, limited to the four attribute bits SetFileAttributes can apply to a directory. ReadOnly is included despite meaning nothing about writability on a directory -- it is the flag Explorer reads for a desktop.ini customised view.
AcceptanceCriteria: A backup of a tree containing an empty directory, a nested empty directory and a Hidden+System folder writes a DIRECTORIES.csv naming exactly those three; restoring recreates both empty directories and returns the folder Hidden+System; a tree with no empty or attributed directory writes no sidecar at all and is byte-identical to a pre-SR-065 store; a store whose sidecar is deleted or replaced with garbage still restores every file and exits 0; the bash restorer creates the directories and logs the attributes as not applied; a snapshot carries the sidecar of the state it preserves, not the live one.

Title: Restored files carry their own modification time
Requirement: Both restorers shall apply each restored file's own LastWriteTimeStr from the manifest row it was restored from, after that file has passed its post-write (Length, xxH2Hash) verification. A blank or unparseable value shall be logged and the row shall still count as restored; the timestamp shall never fail a restore.
Rationale: Attributes and timestamps were never applied from the index -- they rode along on the copy -- so every row sharing one deduplicated pool object restored with the timestamp of whichever file created that object. Reproduced 2026-08-25: two identical files dated 2001 and 2002 both came back dated 2001. LastWriteTimeStr was already in the manifest, correct per row, and simply never read by a restorer, so the timestamp half needs no schema change. The attribute half for FILES remains out of contract (README 'What is not recorded').
AcceptanceCriteria: Two files with identical content and different modification times restore with their OWN times under both restorers, in Plain and Compress; a unique file's time is likewise preserved; a row whose LastWriteTimeStr is blank or garbage restores its bytes, warns, and exits 0.

Title: A transiently unreadable source file is retried, not lost
Requirement: A copy or compress that fails for a reason which could change shall be retried after a short delay, up to three attempts per file, bounded by a per-run retry budget shared across the whole set; a failure that cannot change on a retry shall not consume the budget. A file still unreadable when its attempts are exhausted shall be logged as an error naming the attempt count, shall receive NO manifest row for the content that was not stored, and shall mark the set failed. A file that already had a manifest row from an earlier run shall keep that row, which names bytes the store still holds.
Rationale: The SR-060 candidate loop falls back only to other MEMBERS of a content group, so a file whose content is UNIQUE had exactly one attempt: a momentary antivirus, indexer or editor lock cost it the whole run. Human ruling 2026-08-26, after a shortfall-detection guard was rejected as prone to firing on legitimate bulk deletions: the walk at the start of the run is the authority on what must be stored, and a per-file transient is the thing worth retrying. The per-run budget exists because a systemic failure fails deterministically for every file beneath it, and retrying thousands of those would turn a scheduled run into an hours-long sleep (SN-011).
AcceptanceCriteria: A source file held under an exclusive handle released after the first attempt is backed up successfully, with the retry visible in the log; a permanently unreadable file exhausts its three attempts, marks the set failed, and leaves NO row in the manifest; a directory occupying the destination is refused immediately without consuming a retry; a run whose budget is spent stops waiting, says so, and fails the remaining files without sleeping.

Title: Stored form is decided by the bytes, not the Compressed column
Requirement: Both restorers shall decide whether a stored object holds the row's content raw or as an archive from the OBJECT'S BYTES, for a row resolved through its own DataPath as well as for a hash-recovered one: absence of the 7-Zip signature shall mean raw; presence shall mean an archive UNLESS the object's length equals the row's Length and its own bytes hash to the row's xxH2Hash, which shall mean the row's content is itself an already-compressed file stored raw. The Compressed column shall not be consulted for any correctness decision; it shall remain in the schema and may be used only as an input to the restore capacity ESTIMATE, which is already documented as approximate.
Rationale: The column is a claim about bytes stored apart from them, which is D-1's defect class. SR-050 already made a hash-recovered row trust its locator's PROVEN form, but a row resolved through its own DataPath still took the column's word - the last path by which a wrong column could produce a wrong restore: 7-Zip container bytes written under the real filename with exit 0, or a failed expand of raw bytes. Deriving is cheap because the negative case is a six-byte read and the ambiguous case is bounded by a length comparison. The disambiguation matters because SR-004 does not re-compress an already-compressed SOURCE file, so such an object's bytes ARE an archive while its row correctly says Compressed='No' - and such a source may be named anything, so no extension test can settle it. Get-StorageFormFinding already resolved it this way on the audit side; this brings the restorers into line.
AcceptanceCriteria: A store restores byte-exact through BOTH restorers, in Plain and Compress, with EVERY row's Compressed value flipped; a genuine already-compressed source file stored raw restores byte-exact and is never expanded, with the column both correct and flipped; a stored object whose bytes reproduce neither form still fails loudly as content damage.

Title: Stored-object name grammar
Requirement: A stored data object shall be named "<hash>_<len><ext>", where <hash> is the row's complete 128-bit xxH2Hash encoded base-57 and left-padded to exactly 22 characters, <len> is the row's Length encoded base-57 with NO padding, '_' is the separator, and <ext> is the extension defined by SR-070. The base-57 alphabet shall be the 62 alphanumerics less the visually ambiguous 0, O, I, l and 1, and its first glyph ('2') shall be the zero digit. The encoder shall refuse, rather than truncate, a value too wide for a fixed-width field; the decoder shall refuse a field decoding to 2^128 or more; and exactly one parser shall interpret a name, taking the first 22 characters as the hash field and treating the extension as opaque.
Rationale: WP12. The grammar previously had NO owning requirement - it was stated only in TC-004's Expected - and the 85-glyph alphabet it used cost more than its density bought. '.' in the alphabet meant a stored object could be named as a HIDDEN file, which is what silently emptied the Linux CI pool on 2026-08-23; '-' made a leading dash reachable; a space separator forced quoting on every shell touching the pool; and 16 base-85 characters hold only ~102.5 bits, so the 128-bit hash was silently truncated and no audit could compare a name to its manifest row. Base-57 dissolves the hostile-name classes rather than guarding against them and costs nothing: 57, 58 and 62 all encode 128 bits in 22 characters. Unpadded length is the half that removes the visible run of zero digits the human raised this from. On a case-INSENSITIVE volume the 57 glyphs fold to 34 classes, so a name is worth 111.92 bits there rather than 128 - still well above the 94.12 the old grammar gave (2026-08-27 independent review, T1).
AcceptanceCriteria: A generated name matches ^[2-9A-HJ-NP-Za-km-z]{22}_[2-9A-HJ-NP-Za-km-z]+ followed by an opaque extension; the hash field round-trips to the row's xxH2Hash as all 32 hex digits, including values with leading zeros and with the high bit set; a zero-length object's length field is the single zero digit; an over-wide value throws instead of truncating; a field decoding to 2^128 or more is rejected; and a pre-WP12 base-85 name does not parse.

Title: A stored object carries its source extension, opaquely
Requirement: The extension of a stored object's name shall be the elected owner's source extension verbatim, or '.7z' when this tool compressed it, and shall be treated as OPAQUE: it shall not be constrained to SR-069's alphabet, and it MAY BE EMPTY. A source file with no extension shall be stored and restored like any other. No guard shall classify a store by the characters in an object's extension.
Rationale: Two defects found the same day (2026-08-27). The independent review's T2 showed the ratified SR-061 discriminator - 'an old DataPath contains a space, a new one cannot' - would have REFUSED VALID NEW STORES: Test-PortableRelativePath permits a source named 'signed.foo bar', GetExtension returns '.foo bar', and the stored object inherits it. Reproduced on a live pool. Driver probing that question then found T6, a live production bug: Get-HashSizeFileName's -Extension was [Parameter(Mandatory)], which in PowerShell rejects the empty string, so an extensionless source file (README, LICENSE, Makefile) in a set with CompressEnabled=false FAILED THE ENTIRE BACKUP SET. Invisible with compression on, because an empty extension is not in the non-compressible list so the name becomes '.7z' first - which is why no suite caught it. This requirement exists so neither can be reintroduced by a future guard.
AcceptanceCriteria: An extensionless source file backs up and restores byte-exact through BOTH restorers in Plain AND Compress mode; a source whose extension contains a space, an underscore, brackets or non-ASCII backs up, parses, and restores byte-exact; and neither is classified as a legacy store.

Title: POSIX restore portability beyond GNU
Requirement: reconstruct.sh shall depend on no GNU-specific behaviour along any path a restore takes - file sizes, temporary directories, timestamps, free space, snapshot enumeration and path canonicalisation - so that a userland meeting the DECLARED floor (bash 4+, gawk, xxhsum, and 7z when compressed rows exist) restores identically whether its coreutils are GNU or BSD. Where the floor is not met, or a path cannot be canonicalised, the restorer shall fail loudly with a precondition exit 2 naming the remediation, and shall never report a false content (1), witness (3) or host (4) verdict against an intact backup.
Rationale: The three tool gates make the floor loud, but seven GNU-specific assumptions sat BEHIND them, each with a fallback written for 'the tool is absent' rather than 'the tool differs here'. A userland that cleared the gates - macOS with Homebrew, FreeBSD/TrueNAS - therefore got WRONG ANSWERS, not loud failures: stat -c made an intact manifest fail its witness as 'expected N, found -1' (exit 3), find -printf silently emptied the snapshot pool, mktemp -d failed every compressed row and blamed 7-Zip, and canon() silently returned its raw input, losing the SR-009 guard. A recovery tool that says 'your index is damaged' about a byte-perfect manifest is worse than one that refuses to run.
AcceptanceCriteria: On a userland with BSD coreutils and the declared floor installed, a store restores byte-exact from the backup root and from any snapshot; a manifest with a valid witness verifies; the data pool contains every sibling snapshot; compressed rows expand; each restored file carries its own mtime. A target path that cannot be canonicalised exits 2 naming the reason, and a '..' component is refused rather than reduced.

Title: Double-click restore entry points
Requirement: Each backup root and dated snapshot shall carry a double-clickable restore launcher for Windows (RECONSTRUCT.cmd) and for macOS (RECONSTRUCT.command), each of which starts a restore with NO arguments, returns the SR-040 exit code unchanged to a scripted caller, and holds its window open only when the target was obtained interactively. Neither launcher shall contain restore logic: the macOS launcher delegates to reconstruct.sh and the Windows launcher to RECONSTRUCT.ps1.
Rationale: The moment an operator needs a restore is the worst possible moment to ask them to recall a parameter name (docs/process-options.md, 'recall is still the enemy'). The old RECONSTRUCT.bat was not usable by double-click: it closed its window before the outcome could be read, and reconstruct.sh requires --target-root so a macOS double-click could only ever print usage. A pause in the LAUNCHER cannot be used, because it would also fire for a console-attached automated caller that passes no arguments and hang it without returning its exit code.
AcceptanceCriteria: A no-argument launch opens the folder picker, restores, and holds the window showing the exit code; a launch WITH arguments neither prompts nor holds and returns the SR-040 code to its caller, including from cmd /c and from another batch file. The macOS launcher runs from its own folder rather than the Finder default of $HOME. Double-click on macOS is claimed only for volumes that carry or synthesise the executable bit (FAT/exFAT/NTFS); elsewhere the documented route is 'bash reconstruct.sh --pick-target', which needs no executable bit.

Title: Graphical target selection, never in automation
Requirement: When a restore is started without a target and a desktop session is present, the restorer shall offer a native folder picker; when a console but no desktop is present it shall use the typed prompt; and when NEITHER is present it shall print usage and exit 2 rather than prompt. The decision shall be a pure function of its inputs, separated from the dialog itself, so every branch is testable without a dialog appearing. In the POSIX restorer the picker shall be reachable only through an explicit --pick-target: a missing --target-root without that flag remains usage + exit 2.
Rationale: A picker is the ease-of-access half of SN-035, but a dialog is also a new way to block forever, so it must be reachable ONLY where a prompt was already reachable. Making a missing --target-root open a picker would break the twin contract with -NonInteractive AND create a path CI can never exercise, shipping an unverified interactive path in a recovery tool. Separating the decision from the dialog is what makes the matrix testable at all.
AcceptanceCriteria: -NonInteractive, redirected stdin, and a session with no console or desktop each yield usage + exit 2 with no dialog and no prompt; -NoGui or FILEBACKUP_NO_GUI=1 yields the typed prompt; a cancelled or unavailable picker falls back to the typed prompt (PowerShell) or to usage + exit 2 (bash), never to a default target; --pick-target with a stub picker restores into the chosen folder.

Title: Volume-root pseudo-folders are not data
Requirement: Both the source walk and the restorers' pool scan shall exclude the pseudo-folders Windows creates on every NTFS volume - 'System Volume Information' and '$RECYCLE.BIN' - together with everything beneath them, under TWO conditions that must BOTH hold: the folder sits at the ROOT level, AND that root is itself a filesystem volume root (a drive root or a UNC share root). Their presence shall not mark a backup set failed, shall not contribute files to a manifest, and shall not be reported as a pool read failure. A folder carrying one of these names NESTED inside the tree, or at the root of an ORDINARY directory, remains user data and shall be backed up and restored normally.
Rationale: SR-057 added -Force so hidden files would finally be backed up; that also made these two visible for the first time, and both then misbehaved. 'System Volume Information' carries a Deny ACE even for an administrator, so it was reported as an unreadable directory and the set was MARKED FAILED - meaning a SourcePath of a volume root (D:\) could never report success, on any run, forever, and a scheduled job alerted every time. '$RECYCLE.BIN' is the opposite: it is READABLE by its owner, so deleted files were being enumerated and backed up. On the restore side the same folder counted as a pool read failure and MISCLASSIFIED the outcome: a row whose bytes are genuinely gone was reported as StorageUnreadable / exit 4 ('fix this host and retry') rather than ContentMissing / exit 1, so an SR-040 wrapper would retry forever instead of reporting data loss. An intact store still restored - the locator returns as soon as it finds the bytes and only consults its host issues when it does not - so the defect is one of classification, not of success. All three are false verdicts about a folder that is never the user's data. Root-level-only matches the SR-022/B6 rule already used for infrastructure names. AMENDED 2026-08-28 (independent review, T2): the first implementation applied the exclusion at ANY enumeration root, so backing up an ordinary folder that happened to contain '$RECYCLE.BIN' dropped every file under it from the manifest with no error - a first run would never store them and a later run could treat prior rows as removed. Silent data loss, and the first version of the tests encoded it by using an ordinary folder as the supposed volume root. The volume-root condition is what confines the exclusion to folders that are the VOLUME's rather than the user's.
AcceptanceCriteria: At a genuine volume root: a SourcePath there completes with exit 0 and a manifest, no row exists for anything under either folder, and a NESTED folder of the same name is still backed up. At an ORDINARY root: a folder of either name is backed up in full - nothing is excluded. A restore whose pool root carries an unreadable volume folder and whose content is genuinely missing reports ContentMissing / exit 1, not StorageUnreadable / exit 4. The exclusion is case-insensitive.
Permutations: root=set{volume,ordinary}; location=set{root,nested}; folder=set{System Volume Information,$RECYCLE.BIN}; side=set{backup,restore}

Title: Staging lock ownership and stale reclaim
Requirement: At the moment the backup path takes the staging lock -- immediately after the New-Item that creates Temp without -Force, never before, or the write itself becomes the race -- the system shall record ownership of that lock in a RUN.inprogress file inside Temp, whose name and placement deliberately mirror prune's PRUNE.inprogress so both lock-holders are legible to one reader. The record shall carry SchemaVersion, Kind, a RunId that is a FRESH GUID per acquisition and is the fencing token every later identity check compares against, the set name, host, container id, boot id and pid as DIAGNOSTIC fields only, StartedUtc, HeartbeatIntervalSeconds and StaleAfterSeconds. The content shall be written ONCE and never rewritten, and it shall be published by EXCLUSIVE CREATE: a single FileMode.CreateNew write of RUN.inprogress itself, with no temp file and no rename. AMENDED 2026-08-31 (WP14 §11 R-4): the original publish was a temp write inside Temp plus a non-overwriting File.Move, which on Unix is check-then-rename and therefore not exclusive at all, while its atomic variant needs hard links exFAT does not have -- so on the hub's Linux-over-exFAT stack, the exact deployment this requirement exists to fix, either every publish threw or the theft-window closure was fiction. The temp file it staged was also written into a folder the run may no longer own, and a crash mid-publish left a '.tmp' beside the marker that every later classification reads as HoldsContent -- a NEW permanent wedge. Exclusive creation is exclusive by construction on every platform and filesystem. The torn-read property the atomic publish provided is preserved by the READER instead: a partially written marker is ParseInvalid with a FRESH mtime, which classifies OwnerLive and refuses -- the safe direction. That create shall be EXCLUSIVE: if RUN.inprogress already exists at publish time this run has provably lost the lock to a reclaimer that took the directory inside the create-to-marker window, and it shall abort immediately, touching nothing, logging [SR-075/lock-lost]. LIVENESS shall be carried by the marker's MTIME, never by PID: the writer may be a container sharing neither PID namespace nor host with the reader, and the store may be exFAT. A heartbeat shall touch the marker every 60 s for the whole life of the lock, driven by COMPILED .NET code rather than a PowerShell scriptblock, with its handle kept rooted for the lock's lifetime, and each touch shall be GUARDED BY IDENTITY -- the callback re-reads the marker and touches it only when the RunId matches its own, through the SAME open file handle it verified (AMENDED 2026-08-31, WP14 §11 R-7: closing the file and then touching BY PATH left a window in which a reclaim landing between the two freshened the successor's marker once) -- so no late or queued callback can freshen a successor's record. The FIRST beat shall be performed SYNCHRONOUSLY at start and its effect VERIFIED, the run failing loudly when the touch does not land (AMENDED 2026-08-31, WP14 §11 R-5): a store that accepts the marker write but rejects SetLastWriteTime beats into an error counter nobody reads, the mtime never moves, and after StaleAfterSeconds a LIVE run classifies dead -- the confirmation sample then confirms it, because it looks for change and nothing ever changes. A beat that fails later in the run shall be reported when the heartbeat is stopped. Stopping the heartbeat shall be idempotent and shall DRAIN: it sets the cancellation flag, disposes the timer and waits out any in-flight callback, so no touch can land after Stop returns. All post-acquisition work shall run inside a try/finally whose finally stops and drains the heartbeat. An owner shall be judged DEAD if and only if the marker's mtime is older than the StaleAfterSeconds the RECORD committed to, subject to a reader floor of 1800 s that a future schema may lengthen but never shorten, AND a second sample taken at least one heartbeat interval plus margin later shows the mtime UNCHANGED. That wait shall be max(90 s, the record's own declared HeartbeatIntervalSeconds plus a 30 s margin), the declared value validated as a positive number and capped at 600 s (AMENDED 2026-08-31, WP14 §11 R-6: a future writer with a legitimate 120 s cadence and a behind clock shows no movement inside a 90 s window and would be reclaimed ALIVE; the cap stops a hostile or corrupt record stalling the reclaim path indefinitely). A record that does not parse supplies no cadence and gets the 90 s floor. The confirmation sample is clock-free and is what makes the age test safe. A future-dated mtime shall be treated as fresh. CLASSIFICATION shall be decidable from the disk alone and shall be fail-closed. Enumeration shall be forced, literal-path and error-stopping -- hidden and system entries are content like any other -- and an enumeration, stat or access FAILURE shall never be evidence of emptiness: it classifies Indeterminate and refuses. A Temp that is a reparse point or symlink shall be refused outright, since moving or deleting through one acts on a tree this guard never classified. The verdicts shall be: empty with a STALE directory mtime, reclaim (died inside the create-to-marker window long ago, or predates WP14); empty with a FRESH directory mtime, refuse, because a live run may be inside its own create-to-marker window, which its exclusive publish resolves within microseconds; RUN.inprogress only, stale by age and confirmed, reclaim; RUN.inprogress only, fresh or moving during the confirmation sample, refuse and say truthfully that a run is active; a RUN.inprogress that cannot be PARSED (torn, truncated or an unknown SchemaVersion) falls back to mtime alone with the 1800 s floor and is never an error, a torn record being precisely the signature of a writer that died mid-publish; a RUN.inprogress that cannot be READ at all refuses, absence of evidence not being evidence of death; a PRUNE.inprogress of any age refuses (SR-046 mutual exclusion); any other file or subdirectory refuses, unchanged from before. RECLAIM shall be a MOVE, never a delete in place, and no delete within it shall ever be recursive: (1) classify, taking the confirmation sample on the stale branches; (2) Directory.Move Temp to Temp.stale-<utc>-<8 hex>, refusing on any failure and never retrying in a loop; (2b) re-examine the MOVED folder against the identity the sample classified -- the marker's RunId, or for the empty branch the absence of a marker and the directory's own mtime -- and on any mismatch move it straight BACK to Temp and refuse, keeping it and refusing loudly if the move back fails (AMENDED 2026-08-31, WP14 §11 R-3: Directory.Move is atomic but is bound to a PATH, not to the directory that was classified, so a reclaimer stalled between its confirmation sample and its move can move ANOTHER reclaimer's freshly recreated LIVE Temp aside and then delete its marker-only aside; winner-takes-all holds only for movers racing over the same directory. A second exclusive claim artifact was rejected: it would bring its own staleness and wedge modes and need its own recovery protocol, whereas verify-after-move stays inside the existing primitive set and fails only toward refusal); (3) New-Item Temp and IMMEDIATELY publish this run's own owner record, refusing on either failure and leaving the aside folder in place; (4) RE-ENUMERATE the aside folder, forced and fail-closed, because a frozen-then-resumed owner may have written between the classification and the move -- marker-only deletes the exact marker leaf BY NAME and then deletes the directory NON-RECURSIVELY, empty deletes the directory non-recursively, and anything else or any I/O error KEEPS the folder, logs loudly and prints the README recovery; either delete step failing shall keep the folder and let the run continue. Every cleanup of the staging folder on an early failure shall PROVE ownership before deleting anything -- RUN.inprogress present and carrying this run's RunId, and nothing in the folder beyond that marker and this run's own step-7 staging artifacts (the copied prior MANIFEST.csv, its witness sidecar and DIRECTORIES.csv, each of which still exists in the backup root and is therefore no unique copy of anything) -- and shall then delete only those exact leaves by name, the marker last, plus a NON-RECURSIVE directory delete, keeping the folder and logging [SR-075/lock-lost] on any mismatch, foreign content or I/O doubt, and rethrowing the original failure either way (AMENDED 2026-08-31, WP14 §11 R-1, reproduced live: the early cleanups deleted a PATH recursively, so a run frozen past the threshold whose lock had been reclaimed, resuming and then throwing an ORDINARY error, recursively deleted the SUCCESSOR's staging folder including evicted pool bytes whose only copy it was; the fence catches lock-LOST throws, never an ordinary throw after a silent loss). Because a plain filesystem offers no true lease, the engine shall FENCE the residual two-writer window at FIVE boundaries: before the step-7 staging manifest write, before Move-RemovedFilesToStaging, before Save-SupersededData, before the backup-root MANIFEST.csv publish and its sidecar, and before Complete-ChangeFolder (AMENDED 2026-08-31, WP14 §11 R-2: the authoritative state was published UNFENCED -- the backup-root manifest write sat between the eviction fence and the finalize fence, so a run that lost its lock mid-phase overwrote the successor's live MANIFEST.csv before the finalize fence tripped, and the staging manifest write preceded every fence). At each it shall re-read the marker and compare RunId, and on mismatch abort immediately and CLEAN UP NOTHING, the folder no longer being this run's to delete, logging [SR-075/lock-lost]. An UNREADABLE marker at a fence shall be retried up to three times about 300 ms apart before it is treated as a lost lock, while a RunId MISMATCH aborts on the first read (AMENDED 2026-08-31, WP14 §11 R-8: one SMB or bind-mount blip would otherwise abort a run mid-phase and strand a content-holding Temp -- converting a network hiccup into the class of wedge this requirement removes). The marker shall be removed -- heartbeat stopped, drained, leaf deleted -- immediately before Complete-ChangeFolder, so no RUN.inprogress ever reaches a Snapshot_* folder, where prune's unreferenced-data rail (SR-046) would refuse the snapshot as holding a file its manifest does not name. Each branch shall emit a distinct, greppable token into the set log: [SR-075/reclaimed], [SR-075/owner-live], [SR-075/content-refused], [SR-075/prune-held], [SR-075/lock-lost]. No new exit code shall be introduced.
Rationale: The staging lock is a bare directory whose only release paths are catch blocks, so a run killed from outside holds it forever -- the SR-017 wedge, raised from the HomeHub incident of 2026-08-31. Giving the lock an owner record is not a new idea in this codebase: Remove-BackupSnapshot already does exactly this with PRUNE.inprogress, so the two lock-holders end up legible to the same reader. Every element that looks like over-engineering is here because a cheaper version of it was shown unsafe at plan-stage review by two independent passes. PID is meaningless across a container boundary on an exFAT store, so mtime carries liveness. A single non-atomic write is observably torn by a process that dies mid-write, so the publish is temp-write plus File.Move. The create-to-marker window lets a reclaimer steal a LIVE lock, so the publish is exclusive and the victim aborts, and a markerless Temp is reclaimable only when the directory itself is stale. A computed age compares two clocks and the DANGEROUS direction is the writer being behind -- which would make a live, continuously beating owner look instantly stale to a fast reader -- so a clock-free confirmation sample decides instead, and it absorbs remote-volume metadata caching for free. A PowerShell scriptblock on a Timer.Elapsed handler cannot fire without a runspace and Register-ObjectEvent queues to the pipeline, which is precisely what is blocked while a 100 GB file hashes; the bare-Thread alternative repeats the LLR-073 process kill; so the callback is compiled and its handle rooted, an unrooted timer being collectable and System.Timers.Timer swallowing handler exceptions, which would make a silently dead beat indistinguishable from a healthy one. A late callback could freshen a successor's marker, so touches are identity-guarded and Stop drains. Re-enumerating and then deleting recursively still left a window in which a just-arrived data file was swept up, so the deletes are one named leaf plus a non-recursive directory delete that the filesystem itself fails when anything unexpected is present -- the move-aside is the README's own prescribed safe action, and step 4 is the design's safety proof rather than belt and braces. The threshold asymmetry is total -- too long costs a slower auto-recovery, too short costs stomping a live run -- so 1800 s is a 30x margin and is deliberately not exposed as a knob. What remains, a process frozen past the threshold resurrecting mid-phase, is accepted because the baseline is strictly worse: today that same frozen run races a human performing the README's manual move-aside, with no marker, no fence and no detection at all. The branch tokens exist because the observed failure was a one-second clean-looking abort that no wrapper could alarm on; IF-001 stays a fixed contract and HomeHub keeps alarm policy, so facts go into the log and exit codes are not renumbered.
AcceptanceCriteria: A run killed from outside leaves a Temp holding only its RUN.inprogress; a later run started more than StaleAfterSeconds afterwards takes the confirmation sample, moves the folder to Temp.stale-<utc>-<8 hex>, logs [SR-075/reclaimed], completes with exit 0, and the aside folder is gone. While the first run is ALIVE the second refuses with [SR-075/owner-live] and a message naming the owning host and pid, the time it started and the seconds since its last heartbeat, and the tree is byte-identical before and after. The heartbeat advances the marker's mtime, observed from a SEPARATE process, WHILE a long blocking hash occupies the pipeline, and a callback made to throw neither kills the run nor stops the beat unnoticed. Temp holding a stale marker PLUS a data file, a PRUNE.inprogress, an unreadable marker, hidden or system entries, an enumeration error, or a Temp that is a symlink each refuse with the matching token, move and delete nothing, and leave every file hash-identical. A torn or unknown-schema marker falls back to mtime with the 1800 s floor and still reclaims when stale. Two reclaimers racing one stale lock leave exactly one Temp, carrying the winner's RunId, the loser refusing. A victim paused between New-Item and publish whose directory is reclaimed meanwhile fails its exclusive publish and aborts touching nothing, logging [SR-075/lock-lost]. Data files appearing in the folder between classification and move, or in the aside folder between the step-4 re-enumeration and the delete, each leave the aside folder KEPT with its bytes intact and the recovery text printed. A marker swapped for a different RunId at each of the three fence points aborts the run before that phase mutates the pool and cleans up nothing. A writer clock set behind the reader beyond the threshold, with the owner alive and beating, still refuses. No RUN.inprogress appears in any produced Snapshot_*, on the changed, no-op or first-run path, and such a snapshot prunes without an unreferenced-data refusal. The reclaim is demonstrated end to end on a real exFAT volume under Windows and inside the filebackup:local container on the deployment's Linux-over-exFAT stack.

Title: Measured compressibility gate
Requirement: When CompressEnabled is true the system shall decide the stored form of a NEWLY WRITTEN object from the BYTES rather than from the filename, by a sampled compressibility probe measured in the Engine and composed AFTER the SR-004 extension list. The decision shall be a PURE function of {CompressEnabled, Mode, ListSaysCompress, Length, ProbeMinBytes, SampledBytes, CompressedBytes, Threshold} returning {Compress; Reason} with Reason in {CompressDisabled, ModeOff, BelowFloor, ListExempt, ProbeUnavailable, ProbeCompressible, ProbeIncompressible}, evaluated IN THIS ORDER: (0) CompressEnabled=false -> raw, CompressDisabled, and NOTHING BELOW RUNS - no probe is opened, no 7-Zip is resolved, and a Plain set can never name an object .7z nor record Compressed=Yes; (2) Mode=off -> the list's answer, exactly the pre-WP17 path plus the extensions LLR-004 adds; (3) Length < ProbeMinBytes -> the list's answer, BelowFloor; (4) Mode=excluded-extensions and the list says no -> raw, ListExempt; (5) the probe returned no measurement -> THE LIST'S ANSWER, ProbeUnavailable, with one WARN; (6) CompressedBytes <= (1 - Threshold) x SampledBytes -> compress, ProbeCompressible; (7) otherwise -> raw, ProbeIncompressible. Rule 1 of the drafted order - a name-based override of the measurement - was REMOVED by Owner ruling Q7 (2026-09-01) and no such input exists in any mode: SN-003's acceptance extensions are EXAMPLES of the need, so a .docx over incompressible bytes is stored raw and a .jpg over compressible bytes is stored .7z, both of which serve the need - save more space - better than the example would. The threshold shall be 0.10 and shall be applied to the AGGREGATE of the sampled windows, never to any single window: a multi-gigabyte random file with a 64 KiB text head reads about 0.93 and stays raw, while a file one third of which is text reads about 0.7 and is compressed - an any-sample rule would send the first to 7z -mx=9 whole, which is the defect this requirement exists to remove. The floor shall be 256 KiB (ProbeMinBytes): a file below it shall never be probed and shall take the list's answer in every mode. The probe shall open the source READ-ONLY with FileShare.Read - the same share the hasher and the stored-form sniffer use, so probe success predicts copy success; on WINDOWS that share mode also means the open FAILS while any writer holds the file, so no window can sample a file open for writing, while on POSIX .NET's FileShare is advisory emulation and a non-cooperating writer can change bytes under the sample, against which the probe shall read the file's length and last-write time before and after sampling and shall yield NO measurement when either changed - and shall sample three windows of 256 KiB at Int64 offsets 0, floor((Length - SampleBytes) / 2) and Length - SampleBytes, each filled by an exact-read loop that retries a short read until the window is full or EOF; when Length < Samples x SampleBytes it shall instead take ONE read of the whole file as a single sample. Each window shall be compressed into a counting null sink and its compressed length read AFTER Dispose(), a count taken before the encoder is closed reading short and thereby calling random bytes compressible. A path that cannot be opened shall yield no measurement rather than an error. The probe shall be evaluated LAZILY and MEMOIZED AT GROUP SCOPE: it shall run only on first entry to the write branch of the group copy, never for a prior-backup dedup hit and never for an in-run twin (SR-061 - nothing already stored is ever re-formed), and never more than once per group even when one member's copy fails and a later member succeeds. It shall walk the group's readable CANDIDATES - the owner and then every member, the same list the copy path already tries so a locked owner cannot fail a group a readable twin can serve - and sample the first that opens; only when NONE opens is the decision ProbeUnavailable. The probe shall never fail, slow or misdirect a run beyond its own read cost: every probe I/O shall be wrapped, at most 3 x 256 KiB shall be read per WRITTEN group, no probe read shall be attempted per file or per failed attempt, and the destination shall never be opened. The mode shall be carried by the optional per-set configuration key CompressProbe with the EXACT-LOWERCASE vocabulary off | excluded-extensions | always, defaulting to always, an absent key resolving to always (SR-042 / SR-063). Each written group's decision shall be logged ONCE at DEBUG as 'compress-decision: <rel> <Reason> ratio=<aggregate> windows=<r1,r2,r3>', and the per-set summary shall carry physical-object counters incremented AFTER a successful write: 'Probe stored raw: <n> objects, <bytes>', 'Probe compressed: <n>' and 'Probe reads: <bytes>', the last being the first-run cost figure the operator is owed. Stated as explicit NON-CLAIMS: nothing already stored is re-formed in either direction and there is no migration (SR-061); no restorer is involved and no restore decision changes (SR-050; TC-141 proves restore is insensitive to the Compressed column); NO new exit code is introduced and ConfigVersion stays 2, IF-001 gaining a note only; and the stored filename's extension and the row's Compressed column shall both continue to derive from the ONE decision boolean, so the filename cannot lie (SR-004).
Rationale: The 24-entry extension list decides from the filename alone, and on the production library it missed .z7: 649 genuine 7-Zip archives, 880 GB, 43% of the data, re-compressed with 7-Zip at -mx=9 for a measured 5% gain at roughly 20 minutes of two-core CPU per file - about nine days to save 47 GB. LZMA2's own incompressible-chunk fallback prevents the SPACE penalty and never the TIME penalty, because it decides after the match-finder has run; only the caller can decide before. The list had already been cross-checked against a second list that shared the same blind spot, so maintaining it harder is not the fix - the name is not evidence, and 768 KiB of the actual bytes is. The AGGREGATE rule replaces the drafted any-sample rule on the plan-stage cross-review's argument: any-sample re-creates the review's own failure mode, sending a mostly-random file to -mx=9 because its head happened to be text. Rule 0 is both cross-reviewers' P0: today the CompressEnabled guard lives INSIDE Test-ShouldCompress, so a rule that consulted the probe first would name a .7z object and record Compressed=Yes on a Plain set for which 7-Zip is not even resolved, and the copy path would raw-copy under that lying name. The list-answer fallback rather than a failure keeps the probe structurally incapable of costing a file: a lock costs a decision, never data, which is what keeps unattended runs unattended (SN-011). Laziness and the group-scope memo keep the added read proportional to WRITTEN groups rather than to files or to failed attempts - a naive lazy expression inside the member loop would re-probe and re-WARN for every failing member. Threshold 0.10 and the 256 KiB floor are Owner rulings (Q2/Q3) and live as Engine $script: constants read by tests through InModuleScope rather than as config keys: they are two knobs nobody can measure, while the MODE is the operator's lever. Determinism holds within a run and host - fixed offsets, fixed sample size, fixed codec and level - and the one known limit is stated rather than hidden: a ratio landing inside noise of the threshold could flip across .NET runtime versions, which can only affect an object's FIRST write, and where both outcomes are correct storage forms that restore byte-exact.
AcceptanceCriteria: With CompressEnabled=false, every mode x every extension class (SN-003's example names, listed, unlisted, none) stores raw with Compressed=No and the probe is never called. Under the default mode always, above the 256 KiB floor: random bytes are stored raw; text is stored .7z; a random file with a 64 KiB text head is stored raw; a file one third text is stored .7z; a listed .zip over text is stored .7z and the same .zip over random is stored raw; a .docx over random bytes is stored RAW and a .jpg over text bytes is stored .7z (the Q7 pin); and in EVERY arm the stored filename's extension and the row's Compressed column agree. Under off the same inputs reproduce today's list answer exactly - .7z for the .docx, raw for the .jpg, .7z for a .txt. Under excluded-extensions a listed extension is still exempted while everything the list would compress is probed. Below the floor every mode takes the list's answer. A file smaller than three samples is read exactly ONCE as a single sample; a vanished path and a path held with FileShare.None each yield no measurement; a group in which no member can be opened yields the LIST'S answer plus exactly one WARN and the run still exits 0. Random bytes never measure below 0.98 aggregate, which is what proves the compressed count is taken after Dispose. A prior-backup dedup hit and an in-run twin cause ZERO probe calls; a group whose first member's copy fails and whose second succeeds probes EXACTLY once and warns at most once; a locked owner with a readable twin samples the twin and does not report ProbeUnavailable. One compress-decision line is emitted per written group at DEBUG, and the set summary reports Probe stored raw, Probe compressed and Probe reads. An unchanged v2 configuration loads and resolves CompressProbe to always; a mixed-case "Always", "maybe", a null and a number are each refused with status 2 naming the key, in JSON and in CLIXML alike, creating nothing. -Action Verify over a probe-mixed store reports clean, and Reconstruct.ps1 and reconstruct.sh both reproduce every object byte-exact. The container arm reports the measured Probe reads bytes and the wall time they cost.
